title: Robot arm 2026-08-05 — reconstruction benchmark
lede: A 3D-printed robot arm on a desk, captured as 58 RGB-D keyframes at 4032x3024, run through all three standard routes — TRELLIS (generative), Meshroom/AliceVision (photogrammetry) and 3DGUT (Gaussian splat). The RGB-D fuse row stays retired: it measures desk clutter, not the arm. All meshes are gravity-aligned (Y up) and metric: the RGB-D fuse natively, Meshroom via alignment of its 58 SfM cameras to the session's ARKit poses (mean residual 5.5 mm over a 1 m track).

cards.title: TRELLIS
cards.scale: metric via RGB-D dims (787 x 1061 x 622 mm)
cards.note: Clean isolated arm with invented back-side geometry. Its millimetre labels inherit the fuse's desk-contaminated AABB — treat as approximate.

cards.title: Meshroom / AliceVision
cards.scale: METRIC via ARKit camera track (residual 5.5 mm)
cards.note: 35k landmarks. True photographic texture on real geometry; matte white plastic is still a hard matching surface, so expect gaps on featureless panels.

cards.title: 3DGUT — Gaussian splat
cards.note: The photoreal route: view-dependent appearance, no mesh. Panel build: cropped to the subject, 380k splats, opacity floor 0.06 — orbits smoothly.
